The hidden cost of bad rework

Rework is only cheap when it works the first time

A failed BGA rework costs more than the component: the board, the cycle time, and the next failure it causes. Process control is what separates rework from ruin.

Hand rework is a gamble

Heat guns and manual alignment depend on the operator's hands. Success rates vary — and every miss costs a board.

Uneven heat warps boards

One-sided heating on large boards causes warpage, lifted pads and solder balls that never wet.

Alignment by eye fails

Fine-pitch BGAs cannot be aligned by eye. Off-center placement bridges or skips balls under the package.

Temperature is guesswork

Without a real profile, hot spots burn the board while cold spots make fake joints — both invisible until test.

Reworked boards fail twice

A poor rework often returns to the bench — the same labor cost, a second time, with a worse board.

Customer audits see it all

Documented profiles and repeatable processes are exactly what EMS audits check in rework cells.

Installation guide

From unpacking to first rework in five steps

Installation and operator training are included free with every BGA rework station.

01 · Bench & layout

Place the station on a stable workbench with clearance around the moving head. Provide fume extraction or ventilation above the working area.

02 · Utilities

Connect 220 VAC ±10% mains (single phase, ~5–8 kW depending on model). The vacuum pump and cooling fans are built in; no compressed air is required.

03 · Profiles & calibration

Set the reflow profile (rising and activity temperature segments) per BGA type, verify with the K-type thermocouple, and store the curve.

04 · Trial rework

Rework scrap boards first — check alignment, temperature balance (≤2 °C verified on the SM-650) and placement accuracy before production boards.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training included; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time after handover.

Buyer's FAQ

Questions buyers ask before choosing a rework station

Which rework station should I choose?

Choose the SM-650 vision flagship when boards are large (up to 550×500 mm), mixed, or fine-pitch — the 27× optical vision system and ±0.05 mm placement handle the hardest cases. Choose the SR-430A (or S-B002) when you run dedicated BGA rework cells needing ±0.01 mm CCD alignment. S-B001/S-B006 are cost-effective value stations with the same three-zone heating.

Why is three-zone heating important for BGA rework?

The bottom IR zone preheats the whole board while the top and bottom hot-air zones heat the component area. Even preheating prevents warpage and lifted pads on large boards — the two most common rework failures.

How accurate is the alignment?

The SM-650 places within 0.05 mm using its vision system; the SR-430A and S-B002 align within ±0.01 mm using CCD optical systems with beam split and zoom. Alignment is verified visually before placement, not guessed.

Can the temperature profile be controlled?

Yes. Multi-segment rising and activity temperature segments are programmable (8-stage on the SM-650), with K-type closed-loop control at ±3 °C, real-time curve display, curve analysis and stored profiles for different chip types.

Is it safe and compliant?

All models are CE certified with double over-temperature protection (automatic power-off), password-protected parameters and emergency stop.

How do I get a quote and process recommendation?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your board samples or drawings, package sizes and rework volume. Configuration, quotation and a rework-process recommendation are provided within 24 hours.
